tools.name: cep
tools.description: The addresses of a CEP (Brazilian postal code), with latitude and longitude. We join CNEFE addresses, company records and census sectors. tools.name: proximo
tools.description: The address nearest to a latitude and longitude. A missing or empty value does not become zero. `(0,0)` is in the Gulf of Guinea, and the tool uses it only when you send it.

tools.name: buscar
tools.description: Finds a street by name (or by neighborhood) in Brazil, up to 20 results: one for each street in each city. When the query has a house number that exists, the result has the point of that number.

tools.name: unidades
tools.description: The units at a CEP (apartment, store), with the complement and the type, in pages. The CEP lookup groups the addresses by street and number; this tool returns each unit. Without `logradouro` and `numero`, it pages through the whole CEP.

tools.name: empresas
tools.description: The companies registered at a CEP, up to 50 per page.

tools.name: raio
tools.description: The CEPs within N meters of a point (a CEP, or a latitude and longitude), with the distance and the addresses. Free.

tools.name: consulta_cadastro
tools.description: Name, status, activity and address of a Brazilian company by CNPJ. It does not count against the daily free limit, does not show contacts or partners and runs no extra checks. The origin's protection limit still applies. For sanctions, tax status and a live CNIA check, use consulta_cnpj.

tools.name: consulta_endereco
tools.description: Addresses and companies at a CEP (Brazilian postal code), without counting against the daily free limit. Up to 20 addresses and 20 companies; `pontos_total` has the total number of addresses. The origin's protection limit still applies.

tools.name: consulta_sugerir
tools.description: Suggests up to 8 Brazilian companies for a CNPJ, company name, partner, phone or e-mail, ordered by how well they match. It does not count against the daily free limit and does not show contacts. `incompleto` means one of the sources did not answer.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contact, consulta_comprar · Private data: cep, contact, consulta_cadastro, consulta_sugerir, consulta_cnpj, consulta_planos, consulta_comprar, api_access, api_access_buy, get_api_x402_cnpj_by_cnpj · Public sink: proximo, contact, api_access_buy.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contact, consulta_comprar · Private data: cep, contact, consulta_cadastro, consulta_sugerir, consulta_cnpj, consulta_planos, consulta_comprar, api_access, api_access_buy, get_api_x402_cnpj_by_cnpj · Public sink: proximo, contact, api_access_buy

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "cep" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
